title: Home page: try each scene card style

steps.headline: Slide through the scenes and press one. Which style would you rather live with?
steps.notice: Slide the row sideways. Press a scene, then open the lights arrow and the scenes button to see that only one of them is open at a time. Pressing a scene teaches the card its colours after a moment (in practice mode the lights do not change, so the colours it learns are the room's current ones).
steps.risk: Everything here is practice data; nothing reaches a real light.

variants.label: Gradient cards
variants.summary: Each scene is a small card whose whole face is a soft blend of its colours, name at the bottom with its brightness. A moving scene wears a small Moving tag; the one you used last wears a Last used tag and a bright outline. The row opens already sliding to that one.
variants.risk: The most colourful and quickest to scan, but a scene you have never tried is a plain striped card that says Try it to see its colours, and very pale scenes look washed out.

variants.label: Swatch cards
variants.summary: Calm glass cards: the name on top, a row of round colour dots under it, a thin brightness bar and the percent. Moving scenes carry a small Moving tag; the one used last is outlined and tagged Last used.
variants.risk: Quietest and clearest about exact colours, but the cards are the tallest and the dots are small, so scenes with similar colours look alike at a glance.

variants.label: Light preview cards
variants.summary: Each card is a tiny night-time picture of the room: its lights as glowing dots in the scene's colours, bigger and brighter when the scene is brighter. Name and percent sit underneath.
variants.risk: Shows how the room will feel, not just a palette, but the picture is always dark (even in Crème) and the dots are only a rough idea of where lights sit.
